package.description: Windows privacy and security tool that shows every change first, logs it, and can roll most changes back.

en-US.description: Windows privacy and security tool that shows every change first, logs it, and can roll most changes back.
en-US.longDescription:
RidoGuard is a desktop application for reviewing and changing Windows privacy, security and
performance settings from one place.

It covers telemetry and diagnostic data settings, Windows services, startup programs, removal and
restore of preinstalled Store apps, a per-app firewall, app permissions for the camera, microphone
and location, a hosts file editor, ready-made profiles, and re-applying a profile on a schedule. A
security audit reads antivirus, firewall, UAC, BitLocker and Secure Boot state, and saves it as a
PDF report. Diagnose Device checks interrupt load, cooling, sensors, USB devices,
drivers, drive health, firmware, displays and restore points, can copy a file out of a
restore point, and has a Fix sound button. The Memory screen shows how much RAM each app uses,
and Free RAM frees the Chrome and Edge tabs you are not looking at through the RidoGuard Free RAM
browser extension that ships with it.

Applying a profile shows the list of changes first. Once the list is approved, RidoGuard asks
Windows for a restore point and backs up each registry key before it changes it. The individual
switches take effect at once. Any modification is logged, in the Audit Log and in the Windows
Application event log. Registry, service, startup and power plan changes, and
firewall blocks RidoGuard added, can be rolled back from the Audit Log or with ridoguard
rollback. DNS, hosts file, per-app firewall, permission and policy changes are logged only.

RidoGuard has no account and collects no telemetry or analytics. It checks GitHub for a newer
release when it starts and downloads nothing until you click Download and install. That check can
be switched off on the About screen. Other network activity happens only on screens that need it:
App Installer runs winget, Windows Update checks Microsoft's servers, and blocking a telemetry host
looks up its address. It requires administrator rights to edit system settings, services and
firewall rules.

Builds are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen shows an unknown publisher warning on first
run.
en-US.name: RidoGuard
